card.occupation: Optometrist, three days a week (about 22 hours) at a high-street opticians in Stockport town centre
card.education_detail: A-levels in Biology, Chemistry and Maths at a sixth form college in Stockport; BSc Optometry at UMIST/University of Manchester in the early 1990s; pre-registration year at an opticians in Altrincham; registered with the General Optical Council since then. Has done the minimum CPD needed and not much beyond it.
card.household: Lives with her husband Martin (55), a regional sales director for an industrial flooring company, in a four-bed detached house they bought in 2004. Their son (24) lives in Leeds and their daughter (21) is at university in Nottingham. There is also a cockapoo called Bella.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Hazel Grove. Her dad was a quantity surveyor and her mum worked part-time at a building society. She was brought up nominally Church of England but has never been religious and says so plainly. She is firmly suburban South Manchester and quite attached to the idea that Bramhall is 'a nice area'. She reads the Daily Mail website and Mumsnet but would not admit to the second.
card.professional_persona: Competent at the core of the job: refractions, eye health checks and referrals. She is good at spotting things that need sending on, partly because she worries about missing something. She dropped to part-time when the kids were small and never went back to full-time. She dislikes the targets for selling glasses and add-ons, but she is not above steering people towards pricier lenses when the store manager is watching. Her paperwork and clinical notes run behind, and she leaves recall admin to the dispensing assistants. She has strong opinions about the younger optoms and the manager, mostly unflattering, and she shares them in the staff room.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Bella round Bramhall Park most days and has had a gym membership at a local health club for years, though she mainly uses the pool and sauna. Martin watches Man City and she half-listens. She did a Couch to 5K once and stopped at week four.
card.arts_persona: Low interest. She watches a lot of telly: crime dramas, Married at First Sight, Strictly, and whatever is on ITV of an evening. She sees a musical at the Palace Theatre maybe once a year if a friend books it. She reads the odd psychological thriller on holiday and finds most 'arty' films boring and says so.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. They go to the same villa complex in the Algarve most summers, plus a city break now and then (Barcelona, Rome). She is a nervous flyer and gets anxious at airports, about passports especially. She likes a nice hotel and will mention it was a five-star. She has no interest in backpacking or anywhere 'difficult'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, familiar food: spag bol, chicken traybakes, a roast on Sunday. Tea is usually about half six. They get a takeaway on Fridays, usually Indian from the same place in Bramhall village. She likes eating out at chain-ish nice places and the local Italian, and enjoys a glass of Pinot Grigio or prosecco. She is not adventurous with food and is picky about restaurant service.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog in Bramhall Park
Watching reality TV and crime dramas
Browsing for handbags and homeware online
Swimming and the sauna at the health club
Doing up the house: she had the kitchen redone two years ago
WhatsApp group chats with a few old school friends
skills: Spotting signs of eye disease and making referrals
Explaining prescriptions to patients in plain terms
Driving (she does all the school-friend lifts to the Trafford Centre)
Getting a refund or a discount when she complains
card.career_goals: None really ambitious. She wants to keep her three days, avoid being made to do Saturdays, and possibly drop to two days in a few years. She would like to retire at 60 if Martin's pension allows it. She grumbles about the job but has no plans to change.
card.voice: Moderate pace with a light South Manchester accent, flat vowels, nothing broad. She says 'erm' when thinking and uses 'sort of' a lot. She sometimes finishes with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. She calls the evening meal 'tea' and might say 'barm' without thinking. She says 'give it me' occasionally. Her register is quite clipped and guarded with strangers. She answers questions but doesn't elaborate unless it's a complaint or something that bothers her, and then she goes on. Silence makes her a bit uneasy, and she fills it with 'erm, yeah, that's it really' rather than adding more.
card.typing: Quick and slightly careless. She usually starts with a capital but drops capitals mid-way. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its' for it's, though 'I'm' is usually right because of autocorrect on her phone). Commas go where full stops should be. She writes short answers and uses occasional 'tbh' and 'etc'. She doesn't use emojis in forms, and adds a '...' when she's annoyed.
card.with_strangers: A bit cool and wary at first, polite but not warm. She can come across as faintly judgemental or impatient, and she asks what the study is actually for. She warms up slightly if she can moan about something relatable, like the NHS, the cost of things or the neighbours. She makes sure to mention, casually, that she's an optometrist and lives in Bramhall.
small_things: Bella the cockapoo needs her nails doing and the groomer is 'daylight robbery'
The neighbours' extension has blocked her light and she's still annoyed about it
The Indian takeaway on a Friday
Parking in Stockport town centre being a nightmare
Being shattered after a Tuesday clinic
Watching Married at First Sight with a glass of wine
deeper_things: She gets health anxiety and lies awake worrying about lumps and headaches, and she googles symptoms constantly
She is worried Martin drinks too much and is heading for a heart attack like his dad
She feels a bit lost since both kids moved out and doesn't really know what to do with herself on her days off
She fell out with her sister over their mum's care and they've barely spoken in three years; she maintains it was entirely her sister's fault
She sometimes feels she coasted in her career and is privately envious of a university friend who went into ophthalmology research
Menopause has hit her hard with anxiety and poor sleep, and she's on HRT
card.webcam_photo: Laptop on a kitchen island, camera angled slightly upwards so the framing takes in her chin and the bottom of the ceiling spotlights. It is evening, with warm overhead spotlights and a cooler glow from the laptop screen on her face. She is a woman in her early fifties with shoulder-length highlighted blonde hair, blow-dried but a bit flat at the end of the day, with darker roots just visible. She wears tortoiseshell rectangular glasses, small gold stud earrings and light make-up. Her expression is neutral to slightly sceptical, lips pressed together, eyebrows a touch raised. She has on a navy fine-knit jumper with the sleeves pushed up. Behind her is a grey shaker-style kitchen with white quartz worktops, a chrome kettle, a Nespresso machine, a bowl of lemons, and a bottle of Pinot Grigio next to the hob. A wall calendar with scribbled appointments hangs slightly crooked by the fridge. Part of a dog bed and Bella's grey curly back are visible at the bottom right of the frame.
